q: Your API container uses `DATABASE_URL=postgres://shipit:pw@localhost:5432/shipit`. Postgres runs in another container with `-p 5432:5432`. The API gets `ECONNREFUSED`. Why?
options: Port 5432 is blocked by Docker by default
Postgres needs `--network host` to accept connections
`localhost` inside the API container is the API container itself; it should use the Postgres container's name on a shared user-defined network
The published port should be 15432
explain: Each container has its own network namespace, so `localhost` is the container's own loopback. Put both on the same user-defined network and use `db:5432` (container name + container port). Published host ports don't matter for container-to-container traffic.

q: What does a user-defined bridge network give you that the default `bridge` network doesn't? (select all)
options: Automatic DNS resolution of container names via the embedded DNS server
Isolation from containers that weren't explicitly attached
Higher throughput than host networking
Connecting and disconnecting running containers without restart
explain: User-defined bridges provide embedded DNS (127.0.0.11), isolation, live connect/disconnect and per-network settings. They are not faster than host networking; they add a veth/bridge hop and NAT for published ports.

q: Inside a container on a user-defined network, `/etc/resolv.conf` shows `nameserver 127.0.0.11`. What is that?
options: A bug: DNS will fail because it points at loopback
Docker's embedded DNS server, which resolves container names, aliases and service names and forwards other queries upstream
The IP of the Docker bridge gateway
A CoreDNS sidecar container
explain: Docker intercepts 127.0.0.11 inside the container's namespace and answers from the daemon, which knows the containers and aliases on that network. Misses are forwarded to the host's resolvers.

q: A container is running with `-p 3000:3000`, `docker ps` shows `0.0.0.0:3000->3000/tcp`, the logs say `listening on 127.0.0.1:3000`, but `curl localhost:3000` from your Mac returns connection refused/reset. What's the fix?
options: Restart Docker Desktop
Add `EXPOSE 3000` to the Dockerfile
Make the app listen on `0.0.0.0` inside the container
explain: The app listens on the container's own loopback. Forwarded traffic arrives on the container's `eth0` interface, where nothing is listening. Binding to `0.0.0.0` fixes it. `EXPOSE` is documentation only.

q: On a Linux VM in the cloud, you run `ufw deny 5432` and then `docker run -p 5432:5432 postgres:18`. Is Postgres reachable from the internet (assuming the cloud security group allows it)?
options: Only over IPv6
Only if the userland proxy is disabled
No, ufw blocks it
Yes: Docker's DNAT rules in the `nat` table divert the traffic before it reaches the chains ufw manages
explain: Published ports bypass ufw. Bind to `127.0.0.1`, don't publish internal services, or add rules in the `DOCKER-USER` chain. Cloud security groups sit outside the VM and still filter.

q: Which statements about `-p` / port publishing are true? (select all)
options: `-p 80` publishes container port 80 on a random free host port
On Docker Desktop for Mac, a forwarder on macOS relays published ports into the Linux VM
`-p 127.0.0.1:8080:80` makes the port reachable only from the host itself
`EXPOSE 3000` in a Dockerfile publishes port 3000 to the host
explain: `EXPOSE` is metadata (and input for `-P`). Binding to 127.0.0.1 restricts access to the host; `-p 80` chooses an ephemeral host port (see `docker port`). On a Mac there's an extra hop from macOS into the VM.

q: Your NestJS app runs natively on your Mac on port 4000, and a containerised worker needs to call it. Which hostname should the worker use?
options: `host.docker.internal`
`docker0`
`localhost`
explain: Docker Desktop, OrbStack and Colima resolve `host.docker.internal` to the host. On Linux Engine add `--add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway` (Compose: `extra_hosts`).

q: Your production image has no shell tools. You need to see which ports the running `api` container is listening on and capture its traffic. What's the best approach?
options: `docker exec api apt-get install tcpdump`
`docker run --rm -it --network container:api nicolaka/netshoot`, then `ss -ltnp` and `tcpdump -i eth0`
Rebuild the image with debugging tools
`docker inspect api`
explain: Sharing the target's network namespace gives you its interfaces and sockets with a full toolset, without modifying the app image or container.

q: Three containers share the network alias `search`. What does `dig +short search` return from another container on that network?
options: An error: aliases must be unique
A virtual IP that load-balances with health checks
Only the first container's IP
All three IPs (DNS round-robin)
explain: The embedded DNS returns all matching addresses. There is no virtual IP or health checking on a bridge network; clients pick an address and may cache it. That's what `docker compose --scale` relies on.

q: Which driver would you choose for a batch container that must have no network access at all?
options: `bridge` with `--internal`
`host`
`none`
`macvlan`
explain: `--network none` gives the container only a loopback interface. An `--internal` bridge still allows traffic to other containers on that network.

q: You created `backend` with `docker network create --internal backend` and attached Postgres only to it. Which are true? (select all)
options: Containers on another network can resolve the name `postgres`
Other containers on `backend` can reach Postgres by name
A container attached to both `backend` and a normal network can act as the bridge between tiers
Postgres cannot reach the internet
explain: Internal networks have no external gateway but work normally between members. Names are only resolvable by containers that share a network with the target. Multi-homed containers (like an API on both networks) connect tiers.

q: After connecting to your company VPN, containers can no longer reach some internal company hosts, and `docker network inspect` shows a `192.168.x.0/20` subnet that overlaps the VPN's range. What's the durable fix?
options: Configure `default-address-pools` in the daemon config so Docker allocates non-overlapping subnets, then recreate the networks
Disable the embedded DNS server
Set `--dns 8.8.8.8` on every container
Use `--network host` everywhere
explain: Overlapping subnets make the host route company traffic into the Docker bridge. Setting `default-address-pools` (Docker Desktop: Settings → Docker Engine) avoids collisions for new networks. DNS settings don't fix routing.
